handshake_issues.exploitation: JWT token is logged by every proxy, CDN, load balancer, and server access log in the path. An attacker with read access to any log tier can harvest tokens. Impact: account takeover for any user whose session appears in logs.

message_auth_tests.expected_blocked: Server sends error frame or closes connection with 4003 Forbidden
message_auth_tests.proof_of_bypass: Server delivers notification messages containing user_id:772, invoice details, or unread count for Account_A to Account_B's connection

message_auth_tests.framing: Connect without token query param: GET /ws/notifications HTTP/1.1
message_auth_tests.expected_blocked: HTTP 401 on upgrade handshake or close code 4001 immediately after connect
message_auth_tests.proof_of_bypass: HTTP 101 returned and server pushes notification data to unauthenticated socket

reconnect_attack: Revoke Account_A's token (logout or token rotation endpoint). Verify whether the already-established WebSocket connection continues to receive notification events. If yes: session revocation does not close existing WS connections — attacker who captured the token before revocation retains persistent access.
stop_conditions: Account_B receives a message frame containing user_id:772 or Account_A's private data — this is sufficient proof of channel isolation bypass
summary: JWT token in query string is logged on every hop; established connections survive token revocation; Account_B may subscribe to Account_A's notification channel by manipulating user_id in the subscribe frame
